worst_places.after: **`getImageData` is expensive.** Canvas 2D can render on the GPU. When you ask for raw pixels, the CPU needs them, so the browser must synchronize: it waits for the GPU to finish its current work, then copies the buffer's contents from GPU memory into ordinary process memory. That copy is a synchronization point, and it can cost real time — especially inside a loop that runs on every frame. Calling `getImageData` on every animation frame is a common cause of a sudden drop in FPS (frames per second).

patterns: THE dominant defect, present in all 20 files: the em-dash chain. Almost every explanatory paragraph is ONE sentence that stacks 3-5 independent facts with em-dashes, semicolons and parentheticals, and closes on a 'practical takeaway' clause welded onto the last fact ('...— именно поэтому', '...— worth remembering', '...— that's exactly why'). RU averages 34% over-limit sentences, EN 52%. Nothing technical is lost by splitting at every em-dash/semicolon that joins two independent claims and giving the takeaway its own sentence — this single mechanical pass is the highest-leverage change available in this zone.

EN is not just longer than RU, it is HARDER, and by a consistent factor. Over-limit sentence share is 1.4-1.8x the RU share in 9 of 10 file pairs (03: 34%->59%, 07: 34%->58%, 05: 43%->57%, 01: 36%->52%, 10: 21%->40%). Two causes stack: the ~19% word expansion pushes borderline RU sentences over the limit, and the EN pass systematically substitutes C1 idiom for neutral RU wording — 'bespoke', 'hand-rolled', 'illusory', 'overzealous strictness', 'unsuspecting piece of code', 'earns its place/complexity', 'grinds to a halt', 'tacked on at the end', 'exists purely on paper', 'drop down to raw three.js', 'quieting the GC', 'frame hitches', 'contrasty', 'roughly every other beginner project' (ambiguous: 'each of the others' or 'one in two'?). The RU source is plain in every one of these places; the English adds the difficulty by itself.

Sections open by recapping a DIFFERENT article instead of answering their own heading: 'Статьи 01-02 работают с canvas через высокоуровневые примитивы...', 'Статьи 01-03 — это immediate-mode Canvas 2D...', 'Статьи 01-07 дали инструменты...', 'Статья 02 учит полной очистке...', 'В статье 01 разобрано, что...'. A reader arriving from search gets a paragraph about other articles before the point of this one. The cross-link is worth keeping — it belongs in sentence two, not sentence one.

The prose/code balance inverts exactly where the material is hardest. Articles 01-03, 05 and 06 pair every new concept with a snippet or a ```txt diagram before the next one arrives (D=5). Then 04, 08 and 10 — the three most abstract files — drop to pure prose in their heaviest sections: 'Почему «чистый» WebGL настолько многословен' describes six setup steps with zero code; culling introduces AABB + frustum culling + quadtree in two sentences; all 23 answers in file 10 are single 90-130-word blocks with no snippet, list or diagram, several of them describing code in words ('задать backing store в rect.width * dpr'). The zone already owns a diagram style that works — it just isn't used where it is needed most.

RU carries a thick, file-by-file-inconsistent layer of untranslated and transliterated English: «оверхед», «фолбэк», «boilerplate-кода», «escape hatch», «hit detection», «display-объект», «blend mode», «render pass», «z-order», «layout'ы», «тултипами», «датасетов», «build-vs-buy», «throttling», «layer explosion», «мокать», «клампить», «дополнительная бухгалтерия», plus the apostrophe-declension «draw call'ов / call'ом / call'ами» used dozens of times per file. Two are outright broken: «ретеинд-модель» (07) for the retained-mode the rest of the zone spells in Latin, and «компоузитор-независимый рендеринг» (09, in a table that says 'Compositor' in English one row above). And file 10 still has '## Group 1..7' as its Russian section headings.

Content quality is genuinely high — D=3.9, E=4.1, and no article needs its technical depth, edge cases or examples touched. Scoring policy on rubric A: I did not flag CPU/GPU/PNG/JPEG/fps as needing expansion (universal for a strong junior, and article 04 explicitly explains CPU vs GPU), but did flag AABB/WAAPI/UV/GLSL/PBR/HUD/GC/INP/ARIA/SPA/CAD/DPI.
